summary: Implemented named disposable scopes with reverse-order cleanup, bounded error reports, child scopes/resource inventory and stale scheduled-callback invalidation; a typed action registry with namespaced IDs, availability reasons, optional checked state, argument-schema validation, execution errors and explicit replace/restore ownership; and explicit lazy composition with synthetic capability installers and isolated cleanup. The public setup/execute/register_capability/get_status API and status-only :Workbench command do not implicitly enable Workbench. Configuration accepts only enabled; absent enabled preserves the prior effective state. The command callback loads the public API only when invoked, and the public status path before setup does not load composition or providers. View open/close APIs remain unimplemented until their planned dependent tasks; no placeholder view behavior was introduced.

gates.command: make check-ownership; git diff --check; review the WB-05 module, command and lifecycle changes against docs/CONTRACTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
gates.result: Ownership validation passed for all 9 workbench Lua modules with the dynamic-require allowlist reviewed. WB-05 additions are limited to core scope/actions, explicit composition/public API, the cheap plugin command and their tests/benchmarks. Scopes own and idempotently dispose their resources; capability children own registrations and action handles; cleanup failures are bounded and reported while later disposers continue. No generic global bus, eager provider import, external dependency, hosted CI, Nix/host integration or implicit feature enablement was added.

All 26 mini.test cases passed on both Neovim 0.11.7 and 0.12.4 (9 WB-05 scope/action/composition/API cases, 16 WB-04 model cases and the harness probe). Coverage includes reverse disposal, disposer failure continuation, double disposal, late resource immediate disposal and reported error, live resource inventories, callback cancellation/stale delivery, typed availability reasons, argument schema validation, handler/availability errors, duplicate/replaced action ownership, sibling isolation, partial installer failure cleanup, explicit disabled/enabled setup semantics, dormant public command/API loading, and 100 capability create/dispose cycles returning all inventories to zero.

gates.command: make test; inspect repeated capability disposal, installer-failure rollback, callback invalidation and 100-cycle inventory assertions in tests/runtime/test_core_actions.lua.
gates.result: Resource and action handles are idempotent. A disposed child releases its parent registration; disposing a capability removes only its own action and resources, leaving sibling capabilities effective. Failed capability installation disposes partial registrations and does not publish the capability. Scheduled callbacks canceled directly or invalidated by scope disposal cannot run later, and pending callback inventory returns to zero. One hundred synthetic capability/action register-dispose cycles leave zero app resources, capabilities or actions. A resource registered after scope disposal is disposed immediately and rejected with a structured scope_disposed result.
